comment: Discover extraction: GET /api/discover and its helpers move from server.js to routes/discover.js. Executed only with the owner's OK to Dev, mechanically by tools/refactor/codemods/extract-discover.js (two slices, no rewrites).
sourceRange: Two non-contiguous slices of server.js at the base. (a) 7257-7421 (165 lines): the "// ---- Auto-discovery" header through discoverIp — 4 constants (MIN_SCAN_PREFIX 7284, SKIP_INTERFACE_RE 7326, SKIP_ADDRESS_RE 7330, DISCOVER_PORTS 7396) and 9 functions (ipToInt 7261, intToIp 7268, maskToPrefixLen 7274, parseSubnetSpec 7293, defaultRouteAddress 7339, scanSubnets 7371, localSubnets 7380, discoverAt 7401, discoverIp 7412) with their comments. (b) 7485-7532 (48 lines): the streaming comment and app.get("/api/discover"). Lines 7422-7484 (GET /api/probe-printer, POST /api/test-connection and their comments) are policy-excluded and STAY in server.js, unchanged. Also removed from server.js: lines 13-15 (the dgram require and its two comment lines — dgram's only use is defaultRouteAddress; `os` at line 12 stays, used at 4721/4723/6779). The mapper's 147 = 40 route lines + 107 exclusive-helper code lines (comments/blanks excluded); the 276-line region 7257-7532 includes the 62 excluded lines.

injected.how: parameters of registerDiscoverRoutes(app, { requireAdmin, getConnector, listConnectorTypes }). Only discoverAt, discoverIp and the route use injected names, so only those three are declared inside registerDiscoverRoutes; the four constants and the seven dependency-free functions (ipToInt, intToIp, maskToPrefixLen, parseSubnetSpec, defaultRouteAddress, scanSubnets, localSubnets) stay at module scope with their text unchanged. No module-level dependency slots. No CFG/PRINTERS/FOLDER reads anywhere in the moved code, hence no rewrites.
injected.requiresInModule: const os = require("os"); const dgram = require("dgram"); (dgram's comment from server.js:13-14 moves with it)

exports: module.exports = { registerDiscoverRoutes, _internal: { ipToInt, intToIp, maskToPrefixLen, parseSubnetSpec, defaultRouteAddress, scanSubnets, localSubnets, MIN_SCAN_PREFIX, SKIP_INTERFACE_RE, SKIP_ADDRESS_RE, DISCOVER_PORTS } } — the connectors' existing `_internal` test-seam convention; registerDiscoverRoutes returns nothing (does not repeat the Health pattern the Guardian flagged as F5).
strictMode: routes/discover.js has no "use strict" (server.js is sloppy mode; semantics kept identical).

moduleState.constants: MIN_SCAN_PREFIX, SKIP_INTERFACE_RE, SKIP_ADDRESS_RE, DISCOVER_PORTS at module scope; pure values, no timers, no Maps, no I/O at creation. The boundary owns no mutable state.
moduleState.registration: server.js requires the module and calls registerDiscoverRoutes(app, {...}) at the route's original position (replacing lines 7485-7532), so the Express handler order is unchanged (probe-printer, test-connection, discover, rediscover…). The helper definitions therefore sit later in start-up than before (after the two excluded routes register); nothing between 7422 and 7484 references them (grep-verified) and their creation has no side effect, so this is unobservable — stated for the Guardian.

declaredHarnessNotes.test/discoverySubnets.test.js: line 19: the source text read is routes/discover.js; line 141: inside registerDiscoverRoutes the route ends "\n  });" (without this the slice end is -1 and the text assertion would look at almost the whole file). Every assertion unchanged; the message "must exist in server.js" on line 23 is an assertion line and is deliberately left as it is.
declaredHarnessNotes.test/connectorCoreMethods.test.js: line 29: routes/discover.js joins the scanned sources, so the generated test "server.js checks a connector has discoverAt() before calling it" stays active (the call and its guard move).
declaredHarnessNotes.test/helpers/discoverCode.js: declared helper (Guardian reviews every line): only the header comment, the SERVER→MODULE constant, the unused routeEnd import and loadSource() change. Base: slices server.js into the sandbox where os/dgram/app/requireAdmin/getConnector/listConnectorTypes are globals. Head: runs routes/discover.js in the sandbox with a require() resolving only os and dgram to the same fakes, removes those six globals, calls registerDiscoverRoutes(app, deps), requires it to return nothing, takes the helpers from _internal. test/discoverBehaviour.test.js is not changed.

contractNotes: discover.json: 11 requests, each with a declared expectation; N addresses in batches of 40 = 1 initial + ceil(N/40) progress + 1 done record (/30: 3; bare x.x.x.0: 9). health.json and smoke.json unchanged. NDJSON compared record by record; trackDelays adds 300 ms (the route lookup) to the 25 s Health deadline.
packaging: Dockerfile already has `COPY routes ./routes` (added for Health); pkg follows the require graph (no pkg.scripts entry: not a worker); test/docker.test.js walks server.js's require graph and will see routes/discover.js under the existing COPY. No package.json change. Policy rule 8: real Docker + pkg builds (V12) remain mandatory before deployment, each download/build owner-approved.

reconciliation.note: line numbers at the base; keptBetween = GET /api/probe-printer and POST /api/test-connection with their comments, byte-identical before and after (checked by the codemod). serverLines counts a trailing empty element (7,722 lines of text before).

verifiedBaseline.what: Gate 2 commit: application code identical to production 123470b; pins (24), loader, contract set and NDJSON/expect harness in place. Baseline evidence: pins 24/24; 13/13 mutations detected on base; discover+smoke and health+smoke contract runs stable in all six orderings.

extractionParent: Two different commits, not to be confused. (1) Verification baseline: the Gate 2 commit 7e2cf0008221431268aad5a1c7abb4df8c750fc5 — the application and test files every V1–V11 result and the Guardian review were measured against. (2) The extraction commit's immediate parent: the tooling-only commit that adds this final manifest, the codemod and the identity-check correction with its tests. That commit changes nothing outside tools/refactor/ and scripts/verify-refactor.js, so its application and test files are identical to the verification baseline; the verifier's --base for re-runs may be either.

rollback.beforeCommit: the extraction is uncommitted: `git checkout -- server.js test/discoverySubnets.test.js test/connectorCoreMethods.test.js test/helpers/discoverCode.js && rm routes/discover.js` restores the application and tests exactly and leaves the tooling preparation in place
rollback.afterCommit: `git revert <extraction commit>` (keeps history), or `git reset --keep <the extraction commit's immediate parent>` = the tooling-only commit. Both keep the approved tooling (manifest, codemod, identity correction, Gate 2 pins and harness).
rollback.notThis: `git reset --keep 7e2cf00` would also drop the tooling-only commit — use it only if the tooling preparation itself is to be withdrawn.
rollback.never: production main (123470b) is not touched by any of this; it changes only through a separate release decision

knownToolingLimitations: compareRuns compares logs, files written and audit rows between base1 and head only, and consults base2 for printer requests only when base1 and head differ: a base2 that differed only there would not block. Separate tooling follow-up (recorded 2026-11-16); mitigated here by comparing the three baseline runs in all six orderings.
disconnect handling is pinned in-process only (the harness client cannot abort a request)
concurrency within a batch of 40 is not verified
a successful default-route lookup is covered only by the pins' fake socket (the isolated container has no route)
the connectors' 900 ms fingerprint timeout is not pinned here (connectors do not move)
